title: POC roadmap, stakes and milestone handoff - EmberTech
next_steps: Samir to send POC runbook and gating criteria by 2027-06-09
Jules to propose benchmark script and data ingest checklist by 2027-06-10
EmberTech to grant VPC peering and test account access by 2027-06-14
Schedule mid-point review (week 3) and exec readout (week 6) - dates to confirm
action_items: Samir Patel - share POC runbook + pricing bands - due 2027-06-09
Jules Moreno - deliver benchmark harness + sample curl commands - due 2027-06-10
Diego Alvarez - provide VPC peering details and KMS scope - due 2027-06-14
Marcus Lee - upload 3 sample workloads (chat, summarization, retrieval) to S3 - due 2027-06-11
summary: Kickoff for 6-week POC to validate latency & cost targets across EmberTech workloads; agree access gates, benchmark definitions, mid-point review and exec readout. Primary risks: VPC/KMS delays, dataset transfer size, and baseline model mismatch.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel (Redwood): Good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir, I'm the AE on the engagement, with Jules from our SE team. Um, quick round of intros?
[00:10] Anika Rao (EmberTech): Hi all, Anika here, CTO. Marcus and Diego are with me.
[00:15] Marcus Lee (EmberTech): Marcus, Head of ML, hi.
[00:18] Diego Alvarez (EmberTech): Diego, infra. Quick note: we got two priorities — latency and cost.
[00:25] Samir: Great. High level goal for the POC is to validate that Redwood can serve our real production-ish workloads within 99th percentile latency of ~250ms and cost per 1k tokens at or below our target. We'll map milestones so you have a clean exec readout at the end.
[02:15] Jules Moreno (Redwood SE): Quick clarifier, when you say 250ms 99th do you mean end-to-end from their client to response including network? Or just model inference?
[02:28] Anika: End-to-end, because our app has strict UX SLOs. Ideally testing from region us-west-2.
[03:05] Samir: Makes sense. So we'll run two classes of tests: (1) baseline hosted Redwood model variants in US-WEST and (2) Dedicated sim on an isolated pool to model reserved throughput. For private we can do a separate bench if you want on-prem later.
[04:00] Marcus: Important: our average request is about 420 tokens total, peak concurrency around 160 QPS across 8 endpoints. The cost calc matters for our finance team.
[04:18] Jules: Noted. Can you confirm dataset size for embedding/retrieval?
[04:25] Marcus: Right now corpus is ~1.2TB of text, ~40M rows. We'll sample down to 50M tokens for the POC but want to see caching/kv effects.
[05:00] Diego: Also KMS — our security team requires customer-managed keys and audit logs for all model interactions.
[05:20] Samir: We support KMS integration for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we can do envelope encryption and customer keys via partner KMS — we'll attach the security pack.
[05:45] Anika: We need to see SOC 2 type II evidence and SSO/SAML integration notes.
[06:00] Jules: We'll pull the SOC artifacts and SAML guide, but for the POC we can use temporary SAML test credentials.
[07:30] Samir: Proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week) - kickoff and access gates; Week 1 - baseline ingest + smoke tests; Week 2-3 - bench sprint; Midpoint review end of Week 3 with preliminary results; Week 4-5 - optimizations (quantization, batching, cache configs); Week 6 - exec readout and go/no-go. Does that cadence align with your expectations?
[08:05] Anika: Yes, 6-week feels ok. We prefer exec readout with our COO and head of product present.
[08:30] Marcus: Also we want two sets of pass/fail gates: latency/cost and accuracy/regression on outputs.
[09:10] Samir: Good point — we'll define numerical gates. Example: latency 99th <= 250ms; mean cost per 1k tokens <= $X (we'll propose bands); hallucination/QA — no more than 3% regression on your labeled eval set.
[10:30] Diego: From infra side we need a runbook for VPC peering, firewall ports, and egress expectations.
[11:00] Jules: I'll share a checklist with the exact CIDR ranges, port 443 requirements, and a small agent for log collection. It's lightweight.
[12:00] Anika: On workload sizing, we want two buckets: interactive chat (420 tokens, 60ms per token target) and bulk summarization (2k tokens, batched throughput). Also a retrieval+rerank pipeline.
[13:00] Samir: We'll size based on tokens/s and KV cache hit profiles. For the retrieval path we recommend a small dedicated replica set with cached prefixes to reduce per-request cost.
[14:20] Marcus: Question — how do you simulate real-world tail latencies?
[14:30] Jules: We'll run a closed-loop load generator that replays production traffic shape, including concurrent sessions and prefix reuse to exercise the KV cache. We also include cold-start runs.
[16:00] Diego: For benchmarks we need raw logs, traces, and token-level cost breakdown.
[16:20] Samir: Console gives token-level cost and per-route latency breakdowns; we'll export CSVs and the trace links.
[18:00] Anika: Security review: can Redwood's dedicated instances be placed inside our VPC? We want private IPs and no internet egress for inference nodes.
[18:25] Jules: For Redwood Private yes — fully customer controlled private plane, can be deployed into your VPC. For Dedicated we can offer VPC peering and private networking; some control plane calls still go via our control plane unless fully private deployment is chosen.
[19:10] Anika: Ok log that risk as a decision point. If we can't get private deployment this POC might be limited.
[20:00] Samir: Noted. We'll add a gating decision at Week 1: if the VPC/KMS access isn't approved we pivot to a scoped hosted baseline with synthetic data for latency-only metrics.
[21:15] Marcus: Regarding sample sizes — we want the midpoint to show meaningful trends not just smoke. So suggest at least 10k requests for each workload class under production concurrency.
[22:00] Jules: Agreed, and we'll set up automated dashboards to visualize 50th/95th/99th latencies, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens.
[24:00] Anika: Can you also include model-version regression tests? We don't want quality dips when switching quantized variants.
[24:30] Samir: Absolutely — we'll lock a baseline model and then run A/B between float32 and quantized variants; regression thresholds will be set as part of the runbook.
[25:50] Diego: Data movement — transferring 1.2TB is non-trivial. Is there a lightweight path?
[26:05] Jules: For the POC we recommend a representative subset; we can do streaming ingest or S3 presigned upload. If necessary we can use physical transfer via partner, but that adds time.
[27:30] Marcus: Cost question: if we scale to Dedicated later, what's the expected burn? Rough thumb rule?
[27:50] Samir: We'll surface model-level throughput per GPU and estimated tokens/sec. For your load, preliminary estimate is X GPU-equivalents for 160 QPS at your token distribution; dollar estimate to follow in the runbook.
[29:10] Anika: Who's owning the exec readout? Whose slide deck?
[29:20] Samir: Redwood will draft an exec slide deck summarizing objectives, results, gating decisions, and recommendation. We'll share two days prior to the readout for comments.
[30:00] Marcus: Midpoint review agenda should include: (1) preliminary latency & cost charts, (2) regression vs baseline, (3) list of optimizations applied and their impact.
[31:15] Jules: We'll also include a short bake-off of batching and quant configs and show tradeoffs.
[32:00] Anika: On timelines — we need the POC to be demonstrable to the board in 7 weeks. Can we compress?
[32:20] Samir: We can compress but that increases risk. Alternative is a 4-week rapid path focusing only on latency & cost with synthetic subset, then an optional follow-up expansion. Decision needs sign-off.
[33:10] Marcus: Board wants clear metrics. Let's stick to 6 weeks but try to accelerate access tasks so midpoint falls on Week 2 if possible.
[34:00] Diego: Security will need a timeboxed window to review SOC docs; please add a contact for our security reviewer.
[34:20] Samir: I'll include the security pack and add Jules as technical POC.
[35:00] Anika: Any regulatory constraints around data residency? We operate EU customers, some data must remain in eu-west-1.
[35:15] Jules: We can pin region, and for embeddings we can ensure the data path remains in eu-west-1 for those jobs. We'll document the data flow.
[36:40] Marcus: For success criteria, let's finalize: (a) technical: 99th <= 250ms, cost <= $Y per 1k tokens, regression <= 3% on eval set; (b) infra: VPC/KMS established or scoped hosted fallback; (c) ops: logging and trace exports available for exec readout.
[38:00] Samir: I'll codify those into the runbook with pass/fail gates.
[39:30] Diego: For the bench harness can you use our service account role? We prefer not to share keys, so ideally assume-role via STS.
[40:00] Jules: We'll support assume-role and minimal IAM perms for the duration.
[41:15] Anika: Ok let's call out decision points: D1 - access approved (Week 1), D2 - mid-point go/no-go (end Week 3), D3 - exec recommendation (Week 6).
[42:05] Samir: We'll track those in the runbook and schedule an internal status email every Friday.
[43:20] Marcus: Can you also include a small RACI for stakeholders? Exec readout attendees: COO, Head of Product, CTO.
[44:00] Samir: We'll draft RACI and stakeholder list.
[45:10] Jules: Technical note: to measure prefix caching benefits we'll run two modes: cold cache and warmed cache with realistic TTLs.
[46:30] Diego: One more ops ask — retention period for logs during POC? We need at least 90 days.
[46:45] Samir: We can set retention to 90 days for the POC exports.
[48:00] Anika: All right, let's recap next steps.
[48:10] Samir: Recap: Samir will send the POC runbook + pricing and exec deck template by 2027-06-09; Jules will send benchmark harness and VPC runbook by 2027-06-10; Diego to provide peering details and KMS scope by 2027-06-14; Marcus to upload 3 sample workloads by 2027-06-11. Midpoint review tentatively 2027-06-28, exec readout tentatively 2027-07-12.
[50:30] Anika: Sounds good. Thank you both.
[51:00] Samir: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email and create a shared POC channel for artifacts.
[51:30] Jules: Bye all.
file_notes: Transcript contains occasional ASR artifacts (K V cache vs KV cache), and some names spelled phonetically. This is normal for telephony captures.
